Here is the comment I was initially responding to, for context. This is long, but passionate. I appreciate you hearing me out.

It upset me that this is getting posted everywhere, and in places it doesn't belong.

But after taking the time to read it, I think I get it.

This individual is spamming it everywhere because Voat is in its infancy and adopting a policy like this now would be a great way to set it on a more positive course. Not everyone visits the subs this would be relevant to, but the change would be relevant to everyone in every sub.

I think ignoring negativity and boasting positive things so more people see them is a great principle to have, and I think it's just the right one to help Voat find its place and purpose, alongside its other currently stated virtues of openness and acceptance of all forms of legal discussion.

Yeah, I think upvoats-only would add to this nicely. If there's a reason they restrict them at all, I think that's a pretty clear indication of how powerful and destructive negativity can be.

We come to the Internet to have a positive experience. We want to learn, experience, grow and share. We should support each other in these goals. And those that don't share them, we should ignore. Don't inflict negativity on them or their ideas. Just simply don't support them.

And in doing so, those that share negativity for attention, will cease to exist on this site.

Those that want to bring others down because of a dissimilar viewpoint will cease to exist.

Negativity will cease to exist.

Because what is supported most will be seen most. Reinforced most, which is what good things and learning need to grow.

What is supported least will still be there, ready to be discussed and shared. Those that want to challenge or be challenged intellectually will seek out these different views, and engage in them.

And what is garbage will lie upon the ground where it belongs. Only seen by those that dig for it.

I was working on a project similar to reddit for a bit and was going to go downvote-less actually. My thought process was that downvoting would be replaced with just not upvoting.

For those worried about a lack of user moderation, that's definitely to be considered. I mean, look at the site right now, a lot of people don't have the ability to downvote, but the best content is still at the top. Downvoting just turns into not upvoting, which is much less negative.

Plus, it removes the idea of "downvote brigades" what's going to happen, a "no upvote brigade"? It's just not possible.

I see the other side of the argument too though. Spam and trolls won't be buried as efficiently, that's undeniable, but maybe that's a price worth paying?

I dunno, I'm not sure which is better honestly, but it's definitely something to think about. I think that's something we should reward and encourage as a community, thinking about things with an open mind and discussing them. That alone would make this site and community something special.
